title: Lighthouse sales journey heuristics - seller enablement (draft)
content:
Context:
A compact working guide for SEs and field sellers to run a lightweight 'Lighthouse' pilot with platform and infra teams. The goal is to create a minimal, instrumented pilot that proves latency/cost/resilience storylines within 2-3 sprints and surfaces the right tradeoffs for a customer's integration path (hosted -> dedicated -> private).

Why Lighthouse?
- Quick evidence: short feedback loop to show real token economics and tail-latency behavior on representative workloads.
- Low-friction: pre-packaged telemetry hooks and a fallthrough plan so sellers can demonstrate reliability without heavy infra changes.
- Decision clarity: produce two clear outcomes for customer (scale on hosted with optimizations, reserve Dedicated, or plan Private path).

High-level seller heuristics (one-liners to remember):
- Start with workload signal, not model: capture 100-500 sample calls and measure median and 95/99 latencies under realistic batching.
- Show a route map: present 3 options (hosted fast on-ramps; reserved Dedicated for throughput; Private for regulated data) with clear cost delta per 10K tokens.
- Fail fast to learn: define canary SLA gates at 2% error / 200ms tail-latency and iterate batch/cache settings rather than switching models.

Pre-pilot checklist (what to ask for on day 0):
- API access: customer can send 100-500 real requests or provide telemetry logs/sample traces (preferred).
- Workload profile: avg tokens per request, percent of long (>512) sequences, expected concurrency peaks.
- Success metrics: desired p50/p95 latency, monthly token volume, cost target per 1K tokens, acceptable fallback behavior (e.g. degrade to smaller model).
- Security constraints: PII/regulated fields, need for VPC/private control plane, KMS requirement.

Runbook (3 sprint outline) - concrete steps:
Sprint 0 (prep, 1 week):
- Collect samples, instrument tracing stub (X-Request-Id, route tags).
- Create a short telemetry board (per-route tokens, p50/p95/p99, failures).
- Quick economics: baseline hosted run cost estimate (unoptimized).

Sprint 1 (optics & quick wins, 2 weeks):
- Apply batching suggestions (per Optimize heuristics) and enable prefix caching for stateless calls.
- Re-run samples, capture delta. Use Console to export cost & latency graphs.
- Present initial 3-option route map and recommend 1 stop-gap fallback (lower-capacity cheaper model).

Sprint 2 (stress & resiliency, 2 weeks):
- Inject synthetic concurrency bursts to surface tail latency and cache pressure.
- Validate fallback (automatic variant routing) and canary rollback path.
- Finalize recommendation and next-step contract language for Dedicated or Private if needed.

Sales narrative snippets (short):
- "We can show you real per-call economics in under 10 business days with no infra changes — then pick the scale path that fits your SLA and budget."
- "If latency spikes, we’ll route to a compatible variant and keep your UX live while we diagnose — sellers call this a ‘graceful throttle’."

Demo slide run (7 slides, speaker notes):
1) One-line value + ask (sample: 2-week Lighthouse pilot to prove cost/latency curve)
2) Sample workload & customer goals (show tokens distribution chart)
3) Baseline hosted numbers (p50/p95, cost per 1K tokens)
4) Optimization levers we’ll try (batching, prefix cache, quantization suggestion)
5) Resilience plan (variant routing, canary rollback, multi-region fallback)
6) Outcome decision matrix (hosted optimized vs dedicated vs private)
7) Next steps + contract triggers + quick legal/infra checklist

Quick ROI calc (seller cheat):
- Inputs: monthly tokens, target latency, current infra spend.
- Example shorthand: 5M tokens/mo -> hosted baseline $X -> batching + cache reduces 30% -> estimate Dedicated threshold at Y tokens/mo where reserved commit gives 40% lower unit cost.
(Attach real numbers from Console after Sprint 1 to replace placeholders.)

Common objections & scripts:
- "We can’t share customer payloads." -> "We accept sanitized samples or same-shaped synthetic requests; telemetry + traces are enough to simulate tail behavior."
- "We need on-prem only." -> "We’ll run a Lighthouse on our hosted or Dedicated stack with your sample workloads and produce an ops-ready migration plan and a Private deployment checklist if required."
- "Concerned about accuracy regressions with quantization." -> "We run small eval sets and regression alerts; quantify accuracy delta and only recommend aggressive quantization when deltas are within your acceptance band."

Risk matrix (what to watch for):
- Compliance blockers (high) if customer cannot provide sanitized samples -> escalate to legal with product security template.
- Mis-specified workload -> can mislead costs; require a short validation window with synthetic injection.
- Overpromising throughput without reserved capacity -> include explicit note: hosted can be bursty; Dedicated commitment needed for predictable p99 under sustained load.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a one-click telemetry export template from Console for SEs (ticket: JIRA-4321).
- Add a pre-written legal data handling clause for pilots (confluence:LI-1923).

Appendix (short snippets to copy into outreach emails):
- Subject: Quick Lighthouse pilot to prove inference economics in 10 days
- Body: "Hi <name>, can we run a short Lighthouse pilot using 200 sample calls or shape-equivalent synthetic requests? We’ll instrument p50/p95/p99 and return a short decision memo recommending Hosted/Dedicated/Private with clear cost deltas. No infra changes required to start. — Jordan"

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep slides under 7 and make demo repeatable with a canned sample set.
- Avoid heavy use of the word 'playbook' in customer-facing slides; use 'pilot' or 'Lighthouse'.
- Next internal review: SE sync 2025-03-10.

End of doc.
